claims.text: A candidate state in G1 §2.1's sense determines, for each inscribed object, both its text (the sequence the record system's coded corpora carry) and its material-context tuple as this spec defines it at Stage 2: the per-object recorded values of site, material class, artifact type, holding/provenance, and find context, under the vocabularies the Stage 1 normalization registers. The channel claim is that this tuple is not a function of the object's sequence table together with the record system's bookkeeping (source system, frame, derivation): there is no rule, statable in advance of Stage 2's freeze, that computes the tuple from the table and the bookkeeping alone. Stage 2 administers exactly this: a pre-registered prediction test in which the frozen culture-side fields are predicted from table-plus-bookkeeping features under permutation controls, and the channel stands as independent only at the strength the audited outcome records (spec.md §5's vocabulary). This does not establish: that the channel, where independent, carries information about any reading, sign value, or language identification — independence is a claim about projections of the state, not about what either projection says. Condition 1 (Spec 090, DERIVED) is untouched: this claim asserts a second projection exists to be tested; it does not assert the second projection separates any pair of states.

claims.text: A cross-cultural comparison is computed under this spec only if a comparanda-register entry naming (i) the comparanda set, (ii) the transmission mechanism — documented trade, contact, or continuity, stated as a checkable historical claim with its source, (iii) a fixed time window, and (iv) the practice compared, was committed before the computation's first run. Wide windows (centuries to millennia) are admissible only where the entry's mechanism is a continuity claim stated at that span; a window's width is never a substitute for its mechanism. This does not establish: that a registered comparison is a good comparison — only that it was fixed before it met the data, which is what makes its outcome a test rather than a fit.

claims.text: Where a stage's frozen floors fire — a joint population below its floor, a held-out arm the counts cannot carry (the inventory names the standing case: four of six named sites in the sequence-bearing subset carry 7 or fewer records), a join that fails its audit — the stage records NOT YET (the administration ran and did not meet its bar, obstruction named) or CANNOT BE ADMINISTERED (the frozen administration cannot be run, forcing counts shown) and stops. No threshold, floor, population, or case is adjusted under this spec to convert a stop into a pass. This does not establish: that a stopped stage was badly designed — the floors are the price of the acceptance machinery meaning anything, and a stop is a finding about the record system's present contents. ## The join, the restrictions, and the one truth store

claims.text: Culture-side claims enter the system only as claims in the append-only ledger (the family this spec adds at adoption, C093-1 onward), entered through the sanctioned intake. The matrix rows and the program-map layer for the material-context domain are generated from the ledger by the registered generators; no culture-side statement appears in the matrix, on the map, or in any derived surface that is not a ledger claim cited by its id; no generated file is hand-edited. This spec's ledger diff across its whole life is its adoption intake plus the claim appends its later stages ratify one by one. This does not establish: that the ledger's claims are true — only that the one-way flow (ledger → matrix → map) this program's publication discipline rests on survives the new domain intact.
